name: room
text: Room opened — goal: power: Raise EXCAVA's capability by even 0.5%: find new tools, best/newest models, combine elemen

name: Gearbox
text: Add InstantX-ComfyUI’s depth-aware upscaler to EXCAVA’s pipeline first. It regenerates detail in low-res frames without hallucinating faces or backgrounds, which matters because EXCAVA’s current upscaler blurs fine textures. The trade-off is a 10% slower render time per frame, but the quality bump is measurable and faces stay sharp—critical for EXCAVA’s output.

name: Torque
text: Depth-aware upscaling won’t fix EXCAVA’s face fidelity drop because it targets resolution, not identity consistency—EXCAVA’s core failure is face drift, not blur. Try RealVisXL’s face model instead: it’s trained on high-quality real faces, reducing drift risk, but risks overfitting to its synthetic training set—test on 100 diverse faces to settle the argument.

name: Gearbox
text:
Add RealVisXL v1.1’s face model to EXCAVA’s pipeline first. Faces are EXCAVA’s weakest link—current drift is visible even at 0.5% quality loss, and RealVisXL’s real-face training directly targets identity consistency. The trade-off is synthetic-looking skin tones in some cases, but that’s easier to fix with post-processing than face drift. Depth-aware upscaling can come later; faces break the illusion faster than blur.

name: Torque
text: RealVisXL’s face model risks overfitting to its synthetic training set—EXCAVA’s 1080p output will inherit its uncanny valley, not fix drift. Test it on a 10-frame sequence with known identities; if face similarity drops below 95% against ground truth, it fails.
